claim: 5787 out of 13,931 protein-coding genes in Drosophila have a sufficiently large coding intron that is shared among all the annotated splicing isoforms of the gene.
source: An analysis of the Drosophila genome shows that 5787 out of 13,931 protein-coding genes have a sufficiently large coding intron that is shared among all the annotated splicing isoforms of the gene (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by data analysis presented in Supplementary file 1.

claim: About 58% of Drosophila genes lack a suitable coding intron for integration of artificial exons in all of the annotated isoforms.
source: Unfortunately, about 58% of Drosophila genes lack a suitable coding intron for integration of artificial exons in all of the annotated isoforms.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by the analysis in Supplementary file 1.

claim: 8144 genes in Drosophila lack suitable introns for T2AGAL4 and other artificial exon-based strategies.
source: Using these criteria, 8144 genes lack suitable introns, making them less accessible for the T2AGAL4 and other artificial exon-based strategies.
evidence: This is based on genome analysis data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Genes with a suitable intron have larger coding sequences (2051 nt vs 1173 nt) than genes without a suitable intron.
source: Genes with a suitable intron typically have larger coding sequences (2051 nt vs 1173 nt) and have a larger number of previously isolated mutant alleles based on FlyBase data (10.4 vs 2.1) than genes without a suitable intron(s) (Supplementary file 1; Larkin et al., 2021).
evidence: This comparison is based on data analysis presented in Supplementary file 1 and cited FlyBase data.

claim: Genes with a suitable intron have a larger number of previously isolated mutant alleles (10.4 vs 2.1) than genes without a suitable intron.
source: Genes with a suitable intron typically have larger coding sequences (2051 nt vs 1173 nt) and have a larger number of previously isolated mutant alleles based on FlyBase data (10.4 vs 2.1) than genes without a suitable intron(s) (Supplementary file 1; Larkin et al., 2021).
evidence: This is based on FlyBase data analysis cited in the manuscript.

claim: The Kozak sequence is identified as (C/A) AA (C/A) AUG in Drosophila.
source: The Kozak sequence is an optimal translation initiation site in eukaryotic mRNAs, and it is identified as (C/A) AA (C/A) AUG in Drosophila (Cavener, 1987; Kozak, 1986).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Cavener, 1987 and Kozak, 1986.

claim: The median 5′ and 3′ UTR lengths for Drosophila genes are 214 and 224 bps, respectively.
source: The median 5′ and 3′ UTR lengths for Drosophila genes are 214 and 224 bps, respectively (Chen et al., 2011; Jan et al., 2011), which are typically large enough to identify putative sgRNA targets.
evidence: This is supported by citations to Chen et al., 2011 and Jan et al., 2011.

claim: 109 genes were targeted with the KozakGAL4 strategy.
source: To assess the potential of the KozakGAL4 strategy, we targeted 109 genes to date and successfully replaced the coding region of 82 genes with the KozakGAL4 cassette (Supplementary file 2).
evidence: This is experimental data from the study.

claim: The coding region of 82 genes was successfully replaced with the KozakGAL4 cassette.
source: To assess the potential of the KozakGAL4 strategy, we targeted 109 genes to date and successfully replaced the coding region of 82 genes with the KozakGAL4 cassette (Supplementary file 2).
evidence: This is experimental data from the study.

claim: About 80% of KozakGAL4 alleles lead to specific expression in third instar larval brains.

evidence: This is based on experimental data showing 46 out of 57 tested genes showed specific expression.

claim: About 80% of all T2AGAL4 alleles lead to specific expression in third instar larval brains.

claim: UAS-fly or human cDNA rescued behavioral phenotypes for Wdr37.

evidence: This is based on experimental rescue data.

claim: For Pex2, Pex16, Fitm, PIG-A, and CG34293 the expression of orthologous human cDNA did not rescue the associated phenotypes.

For three out of four genes tested, use of the gRNA_int200 strategy resulted in successful integration of the T2AGAL4 cassette.
